author: claude-code

patch.value: Observed concretely on PR 15. The pi subagent ran just CHANGELOG_DATE=2026-08-15 release-check and reported rc 0. CI ran just release-check with the justfile default and the Release gate aggregate failed. The diff moved five bug-fix entries between an 0.1.0-alpha.1 heading dated 2026-08-15 and one dated 2026-08-07, which reads as section churn rather than as a date disagreement, so the real cause is not obvious from the failure output. Regenerating with the defaults CI uses made changelog-check report up to date. The underlying fragility is that with zero tags in the repository the changelog content is a pure function of a hardcoded constant, and the one documented reason to override that constant is a release run.
release-check passes locally and fails in CI whenever CHANGELOG_DATE is overridden, because this repository has no git tags to date releases from

The justfile hardcodes CHANGELOG_DATE 2026-08-07 and CI runs just release-check with no override, so the committed CHANGELOG.md must be generated at that exact date. This repository has no git tags at all, so --all-release-tags derives no tag windows and every heading is dated purely by --date.

Generating the changelog in a working copy and verifying it in CI cannot disagree; either the date is derived from a real tag, or an overridden CHANGELOG_DATE cannot silently produce a committed file that CI rejects

value.author: claude-code
value.text: The justfile already documents the nested-just override problem for changelog-check. That comment addresses a different failure: it makes a release run verify against the date it generated with. It does not address a contributor overriding the date outside a release, which is what happened here.

value.author: claude-code
value.text: Related fleet-wide pattern: pm-changelog clock dependence has bitten this fleet twice before, once through timezone handling and once through an untagged today-fallback.

value.author: claude-code
value.text: A gate whose verdict changes with no change to its inputs is measuring the clock. Here the input is a hardcoded date constant rather than the wall clock, but the effect on a contributor is identical.
